title: Birthday Party Planning Kit
subtitle: For kids' parties and milestone adult birthdays: 1st, sweet 16, 21st, and every decade from 30 to 90.
intro: A great birthday party is about the person, not the price tag. This kit gives you a timeline, checklists, food amounts, game ideas, and a budget guide for every age from a first birthday to a ninetieth. Pick the sections that fit and skip the rest.

sections.heading: Birthday Party Timeline
sections.note: Spring and early summer fill up quickly in Chicago-area party venues, so book those dates earlier.

tasks: Choose the date and time, avoiding school breaks, holidays, and conflicts with big Chicago events.
Set a budget and decide who is paying for what.
Decide on a theme, color scheme, or activity for the guest of honor.
Make a first-draft guest list and set a maximum headcount.
Tour or book a venue: backyard, banquet hall, park pavilion, restaurant, or party room.
Check park district permit rules and deadlines if you are using a public space.
Book entertainment: DJ, magician, face painter, balloon artist, bounce house, or live music.
Book a photographer or ask a friend to take photos.
Order or choose a cake, cupcakes, or dessert table.
Reserve rentals: tables, chairs, linens, tent, dinnerware, glassware, and lighting.
Send save-the-dates for milestone birthdays or out-of-town guests.
Send invitations by mail, email, or text with an RSVP date.
Plan the menu and decide between catering, takeout, or home cooking.
Order decorations, balloons, banners, and tableware.
Plan the games, activities, or program.
Decide on party favors or goody bags.
Create a playlist with the guest of honor's favorites.
Follow up on RSVPs and note allergies.
Confirm the headcount with the caterer, venue, and rental company.
Buy food, drinks, and supplies that can be stored.
Prepare a slideshow, memory book, or video tribute for milestone events.
Confirm delivery windows and setup time with every vendor.
Check the weather and arrange a tent or indoor space as backup.
Finalize the schedule and share it with helpers.
Assign jobs: greeting guests, cake cutting, music, photos, cleanup.
Buy candles, lighter, and cake knife.
Pick up the gift table items and a card box.
Prepare a rain or cold-weather plan for outdoor parties.
Set up tables, chairs, and decorations if you can access the space.
Prepare make-ahead food and chill drinks.
Charge the camera and speaker.
Confirm rentals will arrive when planned.
Pack a party kit with tape, scissors, trash bags, and wipes.
Receive and inspect rental deliveries.
Finish decorations and food setup an hour before guests arrive.
Set out welcome signs, name tags, and games.
Greet each guest and introduce people who have not met.
Take a group photo near the start of the party before people leave.
Light the candles and sing at the time you planned.
Return or prepare rentals for pickup.
Send thank-you notes or messages within a week.
Share photos with guests.
Pay final vendor balances and tips.
Write down what worked for next year.

groups.title: 1st birthday
items: Keep the party short: 2 hours is plenty, ideally around nap schedules.
Invite family and close friends with babies for a calm, small gathering.
Set up a high chair for the guest of honor and extra seating for adults.
Plan a smash cake for the baby and a regular cake for guests.
Provide a quiet area for nursing, diaper changes, and naps.
Choose soft, safe toys and avoid small parts.

groups.title: Kids 2 to 12
items: Plan 1.5 to 2 hours for young kids, and up to 3 hours for older kids.
Choose one main activity and a backup, such as a bounce house, crafts, or field games.
Ask parents about food allergies and whether they will stay or drop off.
Set up child-sized tables and chairs and a separate adult seating area.
Plan safe spaces for kids to run, with an adult watching each area.
Prepare goody bags and a simple thank-you handout.

groups.title: Sweet 16
items: Ask the guest of honor what vibe they want: dance party, spa day, or dinner.
Book a DJ, photo booth, or videographer.
Create a guest list with a limit and decide whether parents attend.
Plan a candle-lighting ceremony or slideshow if they want one.
Arrange rides or a safe pickup plan for guests.
Set clear rules about phones, alcohol, and curfew.

groups.title: 21st birthday
items: Plan a venue with licensed service and ID checks.
Arrange rideshare, designated drivers, or a shuttle.
Plan food so guests do not drink on empty stomachs.
Offer non-alcoholic options and water.
Choose a few fun toasts or traditions.
Keep photos, cups, and decor within a reasonable budget.

groups.title: Milestone adult birthdays (30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90)
items: Ask the guest of honor what feels right: surprise or planned, big or small.
Gather photos and stories from friends and family for a slideshow or memory book.
Choose seating with easy access, ample lighting, and low noise for older guests.
Arrange accessible parking and a shuttle if needed.
Plan a short, warm toast program rather than a long one.
Use rented comfortable chairs and enough tables so no one has to stand.

sections.heading: Food and Drink Amounts
sections.note: Rough planning quantities for a 2- to 3-hour party. Increase for dinner, longer events, or hearty eaters.
rows: 1 full sheet and a half sheet
2 drinks first hour, 1 per hour after

sections.heading: Games and Activities
items: For toddlers: bubbles, sensory bins, soft blocks, and a simple music-and-dance circle.
For ages 3 to 6: pin the tail, scavenger hunt, musical chairs, and a piñata.
For ages 7 to 12: relay races, sack races, water balloon toss, and capture the flag.
For teens: karaoke, a movie night, a photo booth with props, or a mini tournament.
For sweet 16: a dance floor, a DJ, a candy bar, and a polaroid guest book.
For adults: trivia about the guest of honor, a memory jar, and a toast circle.
Run a this-or-that photo wall with past photos for milestone birthdays.
Set up lawn games such as cornhole, giant Jenga, and bocce for backyard parties.
Have a craft table for younger kids: decorate a cookie, make a crown, or paint a mask.
Keep a quiet corner with coloring pages and books for kids who need a break.
For rainy days: build an indoor obstacle course, hold a dance contest, or run a movie.
Appoint an adult to run each game so the party stays on schedule.

groups.title: Seating and tables
items: Order one adult chair for every adult guest.
Add kid-sized tables and chairs for children under 7.
Add a cake table, gift table, and drink station.
Order cocktail tables for mingling at adult parties.
Choose tablecloths in the party colors.

groups.title: Weather and ambiance
items: Rent a tent for backyard parties from May through October.
Rent heaters for spring and fall evenings.
Order string lights or lanterns for evening gatherings.
Add a dance floor for teen and adult dance parties.
Ask the rental company about fans for hot afternoons.

groups.title: Tableware
items: Rent plates, forks, and glasses to avoid disposable waste.
Order serving platters and chafing dishes if you are self-catering.
Add pitchers and drink dispensers.
Order extra napkins for cake and messy foods.

sections.heading: Birthday Budget Split
sections.note: Rough guide. Chicago-area prices vary widely by venue and guest count.

lines.tip: A backyard can cut this by half, but plan for tent and chair rentals.
Order cake and desserts early and ask the caterer to pack leftovers.
Buy non-alcoholic drinks in bulk and rent a drink dispenser.
Book one memorable activity rather than many small ones.
Use digital invitations and reusable decor.
Ask a talented friend or hire a photographer for an hour.
Skip favors or choose something useful.
Keep a cushion for extra guests and weather changes.
